prompts.prompt:
STYLE LOCK — Crystal Quest Painterly World Map.
Use the attached chapter-1-library-map.webp as the authoritative STYLE reference. Match its rendering, color relationships, material treatment, detail density and atmospheric depth, not its specific library building or geography.
Create a finely hand-painted premium fantasy mobile RPG world map. Use soft controlled painterly brush texture, delicate colored edges without black outlines, dimensional cream stone, naturally layered cliffs, nuanced lush foliage, tiny flowers and climbing ivy. Use warm sunlight, cool teal-violet shadows, golden paths, turquoise water where appropriate, blue atmospheric distance and softly billowing white clouds. Violet-blue crystals have translucent faceted surfaces, white highlights and restrained magical glow; gold is a restrained waypoint accent.
Use an elevated three-quarter map view, clear destination architecture, readable winding routes, crisp nearby terrain and softer lower-contrast distant scenery. Keep navigation landmarks distinct at portrait mobile size. The image must look like another region painted by the same artist as the style reference. Preserve the region's own subject and geography rather than copying the reference's buildings.


Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: Wordoria Crystal Quest story world map, contiguous portrait scroll panel 1 of 4.
Scene: "The Last Transport of Fallen Star Fortress." Bright old mountain supply road on an airy lush plateau, worn wheel ruts, small abandoned wooden repair cart, cream stone retaining walls and distant fortress parapets along sides. This is the TOP quarter of a very tall map. The route ENTERS from top CENTER and EXITS bottom CENTER, with compatible golden road at both edges. No large building across route. Regional progression in the full scroll is old supply road -> unloading yard -> chained gate at halfway -> upper maintenance walkways -> transport courtyard -> east gate at bottom.
Reference roles: Image 1 = authoritative painterly style only. Do not copy library buildings.
Composition: 1024x1536 portrait panel, full bleed scene. IMPORTANT exactly ELEVEN individual violet-blue crystal waypoints, one per consecutive horizontal band. Make crystals 50 pixels tall and circular gold pedestal 70 pixels wide at this resolution. Each waypoint separated by roughly130px vertical distance. Scenic land spreads to both edges. Route snakes gently.
Gameplay contract: exactly 11 distinct violet-blue crystal waypoints on gold-rimmed circular pedestals. Stage order and normalized centers, left-to-right x and top-to-bottom y percentages: stage 1: (50%,5%); stage 2: (70%,14%); stage 3: (76%,23%); stage 4: (58%,32%); stage 5: (34%,41%); stage 6: (24%,50%); stage 7: (36%,59%); stage 8: (60%,68%); stage 9: (76%,77%); stage 10: (64%,86%); stage 11: (50%,95%). These are world stages1-11. Build one continuous broad golden path through all centers in that order, NEVER retracing upward. Every waypoint center y strictly increases; no side branches or extra pedestals. The first crystal sits near the TOP; the last near BOTTOM. Crystal pedestal centers are the stated positions. Keep road broad enough for a game button, unobscured by plants. No text at all. NO NUMBERS.
Avoid coarse low-poly geometry, chunky toy-like 3D rendering, plastic surfaces, flat oversaturated green terrain, black cartoon outlines, pixel art, gritty photorealism, muddy dark palettes, excessive bloom and repetitive noisy detail. No characters, monsters, text, letters, numbers, UI, labels, logos, watermark, frames or black side borders. Do not obscure the route or waypoint crystals with foliage, clouds or effects. Do not introduce buildings or narrative elements unrelated to the requested world.
